title: Intermittent session propagation delay causes temporary namespace denial for Dedicated/Private customers
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported intermittent 403s when hitting the Redwood inference API shortly after a node failover or during autoscale events. The errors present as namespace/org-level authorization denials (403) even though API keys belong to the correct org and previously worked. Scope: Affects Dedicated pools and Private VPC installs with the new session-syncer introduced in runtime-1.20. Not observed for Hosted customers in the short term, but path is shared in some control-plane flows. Timeline: First customer escalation reported 2025-02-10 03:40 UTC. Reproducible window observed 1-2 minutes post failover under moderate traffic. Root cause hypothesis: Session propagation (session-syncer) relies on eventual state in the distributed org-affinity cache. Under concurrent node drain + token refresh events, there is a race where the apikey->namespace binding is briefly missing on newly promoted nodes. This leads to authz checks falling back to default deny until the cache warms (TTL refresh). Contributing factors: 1) short-lived in-memory cache warm-up on promoted nodes, 2) token refresh requests that rebind sessions using an outdated routing header, 3) the failover path currently does not prime the namespace-affinity cache for keys in flight. Immediate mitigation taken: - Scoped rollout to pause autoscale-driven node drains for affected Dedicated customers overnight. - Emergency hotfix: added a conservative cache-warm path in the ingress layer to consult the central control-plane before denying requests (temporary, increases latency). Long-term fix: 1) make session-syncer pre-populate namespace bindings during drain/lead-change, 2) make authz check fallback query the central authoritative binding store (fast path) during warm-up, 3) add stronger invariants to token refresh flow to carry canonical org-scoped headers. Impact: Customer-facing 403s (intermittent) causing failed inference calls; impacted customers reported degraded product experience for 30s-2m windows. No evidence of cross-tenant data access. Regressions: Regression introduced in runtime-1.20 when session-syncer changed local-only cache semantics to eventual-sync to improve scale; this exposed a warm-up window. Reproduction steps: 1) Configure Dedicated pool with two nodes and enable autoscale. 2) Create an API key scoped to org: redwood-inc-test. 3) Send sustained traffic, then trigger a node drain. 4) Observe 403 responses on the promoted node for ~30-90s before cache warms. Observed logs: authn-service logs show "missing-affinity" followed by a cache-fill later. Metrics: spike in authz_denied.rate and authz_cache_miss.rate around failover windows. Next steps: - Complete PR implementing pre-populate + fast-path control-plane lookup (ENG-84567-PR). - Add e2e test to the chaos suite to validate no authorization gaps during node failover. - Post-fix gradual rollout with enhanced telemetry and customer-specific opt-in for private installs.
comments: 2025-02-12: Initial triage by on-call. Reproduced in staging by simulating node drain. Assigned to Marcus.
2025-02-13: Implemented temporary ingress consult fallback to prevent denies; latency increase ~12ms P95. Deployed to impacted Dedicated customers as immediate mitigation.
2025-02-14: Root cause analysis completed. Proposed fix to pre-populate cache and add fast-path control-plane read approved by security and infra leads.
2025-02-15: PR ENG-84567-PR opened (runtime, session-syncer). QA added e2e chaos test tickets. Planning canary rollout for 2025-02-18.
acceptance_criteria: No 403 spikes observed in canary after failover in chaos e2e suite for sustained traffic
No increased latency beyond current SLO when fast-path control-plane lookup is used
PR reviewed and security sign-off completed for Private/VPC considerations
